To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Pax gene Poxm plays an important role in myogenesis, and has both early and late functions.

Poxm has two distinct functions during myogenesis, that it is one the crucial genes regulating somatic muscle development and that it is a major regulator of the expression of the muscle determination genes l(1)scarlet and twist.

Pox meso has two distinct and partially redundant functions in somatic myoblast determination and muscle identity specification, and that these two functions are expressed during two distinct and consecutive phases of myogenesis, early and late.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the body wall musculature of Drosophilas, and the role of Pax genes therein.
the molecular mechanisms that govern myogenesis in Drosophia melanogaster.
the role of Pax genes in the development of the body wall muscle system in Drosophla.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Poxm and l(1)sch have two distinct functions during myogenesis: an early function in demarcating the `Pox competence domain' and a late function in the specification of muscle identities.
the Pox meso gene plays a key role in the development of Drosophia body wall musculature.
Poxm is a key regulator of somatic myogenesis in Drosophla.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pax genes are involved in all three phases of myogenesis: determination of the mesodermal precursor cells, specification of the muscle precursor cells and specification of the adult muscles.
the early function of Poxm and l(1)sch is required to define the `Pox competence domain' and the later function of Pox m is required for the specification and/or maintenance of the muscle identities.
Poxm and l(1)sec act together to specify the Poxm competence domain, and then Poxm acts alone to specify the identity of a subset of the muscle precursors within this domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Poxm is one of the key genes regulating the development, identity and pattern of the larval and adult body wall muscles.
the Pox genes have a much more diverse function in myogenesis than was previously assumed.
Poxm is a key regulator of myogenesis in Drosophlia.
